evidence.claims: Disclaimer, assumed-constant labelling, single-pose and planar limits and the cost-as-lower-bound are honest and backed. Failing claims: README:26 'damping ratio held at 1.28 ... so only the mass changes' is false: holding zeta makes kd scale with sqrt(m), so the free approach speed at the nominal 0.20 m/s is KP*LEAD*v/kd = 0.143 (0.30 kg), 0.110 (6 joints), 0.099 m/s (2 joints), and the linear-spring impact estimate v*sqrt(K*m) is 2.213 N for every mass: the mass-invariance of lip force is built in by the gain rule (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/607d6f8f-15aa-5946-acd2-45d53e86ef9e/scratchpad/dof/confound.py). With osrobot-assist's actual fixed kd=28, worst peak rises 4.00 -> 4.07 -> 4.25 N and safe share 0.71 -> 0.67 -> 0.65 with mass. README:9 calls Lambda_xx 'the effective mass at the spoon tip along the approach direction'; the directional effective mass 1/(x^T Lambda^-1 x) is 0.58/0.50/0.54/0.40/0.43 kg (7-19% lower). The 'speed' column is nominal, not the approach speed, and the 1.7x longer feed time (1.47 vs 0.88 s) is not mentioned. README:18 '20 s' stale. Numbers backed, the causal reading not: 2.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could reuse tip_mass (correct, verified two ways) as a small planar Lambda calculator. The headline result cannot be built on as stated: the lip-force null across joint counts follows from the constant-damping-ratio gain rule, and the worst peak 4.0 N is the static stall push KP*LEAD*v (independent of mass by construction; it also coincides with the X_DEPTH equilibrium 400*800*0.015/1200 = 4.0 N). Nearest prior work, none cited: Khatib (1995) 'Inertial properties in robotic manipulation' (directional effective mass), Haddadin et al. (2009, 2012) on effective mass and reflected inertia in impact safety, ISO/TS 15066 transient-contact effective mass, Wensing et al. (2017) on reflected inertia scaling with gear ratio squared, and low-DOF feeding devices (Obi, My Spoon, Bestic) versus 6/7-DOF arms in ADA/Kinova feeding work (Bhattacharjee et al. 2020; Park et al. 2020). 'Reflected rotor inertia dominates effective mass in highly geared servos' is well known; the result is sound as arithmetic, not new, and the comparative claim is confounded: 1.
evidence.domain: Compared against operational-space dynamics practice (Khatib 1987/1995) and pHRI impact analysis (Haddadin; ISO/TS 15066). Correct: Lambda=(J M^-1 J^T)^-1 for a planar chain, reflected inertia N^2*I_rotor on the joint diagonal, Hunt-Crossley F = K x (1 + C v) (the n=1 form, k x^n + lambda x^n xdot with lambda=C*K), SO-ARM-class 345:1 servo. Departures: Lambda_xx (y held rigid) used where the free-direction effective mass 1/(u^T Lambda^-1 u) is standard for a 1-D impact; gains rescaled with mass so the controller, not the arm, sets the impact; rotor inertia 1e-7 unsourced although it sets 80% of the mass; one pose. A practitioner would accept the mass model with these caveats, not the lip-force conclusion: 2.

defects.what: The lip-force comparison is confounded by the gain rule: damping ratio held at 1.28 makes kd scale with sqrt(m), so the free approach speed falls as 1/sqrt(m) (0.143 -> 0.099 m/s at a nominal 0.20) and the impact estimate v*sqrt(K m) is exactly mass-invariant (2.213 N); 'extra joints do not change lip force' is built in, and README:26 'so only the mass changes' is false. With fixed gains (kd=28) worst peak 4.00 -> 4.25 N, safe 0.71 -> 0.65

4 of 5 seeded core mutations survive (reflected inertia N instead of N^2, Lambda_yy for Lambda_xx, kd ignoring mass, servo position); the only numeric test uses an isotropic spoon-only case that cannot distinguish x from y or check any rotor/servo term

Lambda_xx (y held rigid) reported as 'the effective mass along the approach direction'; the directional effective mass 1/(x^T Lambda^-1 x) (Khatib 1995, ISO/TS 15066 practice) is 7-19% lower (0.58 vs 0.63 kg for 2 joints, 0.40 vs 0.49 for 5)

No prior work on effective mass and reflected inertia in impact safety (Khatib 1995, Haddadin et al., ISO/TS 15066, Wensing et al. 2017) or on low-DOF vs 6/7-DOF feeding devices (Obi, My Spoon, Bestic, ADA/Kinova) is cited; the 'mass is mostly the gearbox' finding is well known

verdict: Every number reproduces byte-for-byte, and the tip masses agree with an independent closed-form 2R calculation (0.6280 kg at 345^2 x 1e-7 = 0.0119 kg m^2) and an independent finite-difference n-link calculation to four decimals; the servo arithmetic, the $26.00 price and the 0.03 standard error check out. But the headline, that joint count does not change lip force, is largely built in: holding the damping ratio constant makes the actual approach speed fall as 1/sqrt(mass), which cancels mass out of the impact force exactly; with osrobot-assist's fixed gains the heavier arms do push harder (4.00 -> 4.25 N worst, safe 0.71 -> 0.65). The reported mass is Lambda_xx rather than the directional effective mass (7-19% lower), the tests let 4 of 5 core mutations through, and no effective-mass, impact-safety or feeding-device prior work is cited. Finished as scoped; below the bar on verification, claims, fitness and domain.
